metadata.title: The outer-pedal area centroid in even-period elliptic billiards
metadata.description: We prove the k307 outer-side pedal area-centroid observation of Reznik, Garcia and Koiller for billiards in a noncircular ellipse with a strict confocal elliptic caustic and least even period. The ordered perpendicular feet of any fixed point on the boundary tangent lines have an explicit phase-independent signed area centroid wherever their signed area is nonzero. We classify the entire zero-area locus: none when d is nonnegative, and a fixed circle when d is negative. Simple winding-one even families have a centroid for every fixed point; the four-period value is M/3. An exact primitive eight-period star shows that the exceptional undefined locus is real. The note supplies an all-period support-coordinate and cubic-moment proof. The verification archive contains the LaTeX source, exact symbolic and rational certificates, independent high-precision orbit controls, audit reports and reproducibility instructions. The original observation and classical methods are credited. Bounded primary-source audits found no earlier covering proof, without certifying historical firstness. AI tools were used extensively in solving, verifying, literature research, writing and adversarial review. This is an unrefereed preprint and has not received external human peer review or proof-assistant formalization.

metadata.title: L2-acyclicity and cost for a rank-100 amalgam
metadata.description:
An expanded consequence and verification note for OpenAI's rank-100 fixed-price construction. A self-contained regular-tree and cellular-boundary calculation proves that its displayed 101-generator/100-relator presentation complex is a finite two-dimensional classifying space and every L2-Betti number vanishes, independently of either cost bound. Gaboriau's action invariance and OpenAI's positive Bernoulli cost estimate then give an explicit free ergodic p.m.p. orbit relation with Cost at least 1 + 1/(100*2^61) and vanishing L2-Betti numbers. The group infimum cost is one.

The group and positive cost estimate are due to OpenAI; cost--Betti comparison and action invariance are due to Gaboriau. The general fixed-price implication was already explicit in Popa--Shlyakhtenko--Vaes, and the short conditional limit argument was already in the author's public preliminary triage. Added content is the direct all-degree invariant proof and reproducible input-validation record. No independent fixed-price discovery or firstness is claimed. The pinned upstream source warns that its source argument was intermediate. Its pivotal proof is explicitly identified and independently audited in the supplement.

AI tools were used extensively in research, drafting and adversarial verification. At publication this preprint has not undergone conventional human peer review or refereeing. Automated audits are neither human refereeing nor machine formalization. The package contains the paper source, exact arithmetic and Fox-identity checks, scoped proof audits, source hashes, priority record and clean reproduction instructions.

metadata.title: Bilinear ergodic Hilbert variation for commuting transformations as a consequence of annular triangular variation
metadata.description: We give an explicit restriction and transference consequence of OpenAI's full annular variation theorem for the triangular Hilbert transform, manuscript dated October 5, 2026, at source commit adc7f1241b42e322a6451854ab7e4b4c146bf78a. For arbitrary commuting invertible probability-preserving transformations S,T and complex f,g in L3, the symmetric sums H_N=sum_(0<|n|<=N) f(S^n x)g(T^n x)/n, with H_0=0, satisfy a pointwise r-variation estimate in L^(3/2) for every r>2. They have a bounded maximum and converge almost everywhere and in L^(3/2), with maximal-tail convergence in that norm. The proof uses fixed positive-area cell boxes, half-integer radial endpoints, an explicitly summable O(k^-2) signed kernel error, and finite-menu finite-window Calderon transference. The continuous analytic breakthrough is inherited and credited; this note supplies its discrete restriction and ergodic consequence. Classical transference and its modern predecessors are credited, and no first-priority or independent triangular-Hilbert breakthrough claim is made. Scope remains L3 inputs, symmetric odd truncations, commuting transformations and r>2; there is no r=2, noncommuting or one-sided Cesaro claim. AI tools were used extensively in research, drafting and verification. Automated adversarial audits are not human peer review or formal certification. The relevant Lean artifacts concern an older maximal theorem and do not formally verify full annular variation or this note. This preprint has not undergone conventional human peer review or refereeing at publication.
